claim: Human fertility is suboptimal in part due to error-prone divisions during early cleavage stages, which frequently result in chromosomal aneuploidy.
source: Human fertility is suboptimal in part by error-prone divisions during early cleavage stages, which frequently result in chromosomal aneuploidy.
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract that draws on established scientific understanding about human fertility and aneuploidy.

claim: Most human pre-implantation embryos are mosaics of euploid and aneuploid cells.
source: Most human pre-implantation embryos are mosaics of euploid and aneuploid cells, yet those with a low proportion of aneuploid cells can develop to term at rates similar to fully euploid embryos.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations in the introduction section.

claim: Human pre-implantation embryos with a low proportion of aneuploid cells can develop to term at rates similar to fully euploid embryos.
source: Most human pre-implantation embryos are mosaics of euploid and aneuploid cells, yet those with a low proportion of aneuploid cells can develop to term at rates similar to fully euploid embryos.
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research on mosaic embryo outcomes.

claim: The Mps1 inhibitor AZ3146 disrupts chromosome segregation but supports higher developmental potential than reversine.
source: Here, we demonstrate that the more specific Mps1 inhibitor AZ3146 similarly disrupts chromosome segregation but supports higher developmental potential than reversine.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data including embryo transfer experiments and cell counts.

claim: AZ3146-treated embryos transiently upregulate hypoxia-inducible factor-1A (HIF1A) without triggering Trp53 activation.
source: AZ3146-treated embryos transiently upregulate hypoxia-inducible factor-1A (HIF1A) without triggering Trp53 activation.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR and immunofluorescence data presented in Figure 2.

claim: Hypoxia exposure in vitro reduced DNA damage in response to Mps1 inhibition.
source: Hypoxia exposure in vitro reduced DNA damage in response to Mps1 inhibition and increased the proportion of euploid cells in mosaic epiblast.
evidence: This is supported by γH2A.X intensity measurements in embryos cultured under hypoxic conditions.

claim: Hypoxia exposure increased the proportion of euploid cells in mosaic epiblast.
source: Hypoxia exposure in vitro reduced DNA damage in response to Mps1 inhibition and increased the proportion of euploid cells in mosaic epiblast.
evidence: This is supported by lineage allocation data from chimeric embryos cultured in hypoxia.

claim: HIF1A inhibition decreased the proportion of aneuploid cells in mosaic embryos.
source: Conversely, HIF1A inhibition decreased the proportion of aneuploid cells.
evidence: This is supported by data from IDF-11774 treatment experiments in chimeric embryos.

claim: Only ~30% of human conceptions result in live birth.
source: Humans have relatively low fertility compared to other mammals, with only ~30% of conceptions resulting in live birth (Palmerola et al., 2022; Capalbo et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a cited statistic from published literature.

claim: It is estimated that ~60% of pre-implantation IVF embryos exhibit chromosomal mosaicism.
source: It is estimated that ~60% of pre-implantation IVF embryos exhibit this form of mosaicism (Capalbo et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a cited statistic from published literature.

claim: The incidence of aneuploidy declines as development progresses.
source: The incidence of aneuploidy declines as development progresses (Shahbazi et al., 2020; Yang et al., 2021), but the mechanism underlying this decline remains unclear.
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Embryos classified as low- or medium-grade mosaics have implantation and birth rates comparable to fully euploid embryos.
source: Specifically, embryos classified as low- or medium-grade mosaics – defined by the presence of 20–30% or 30–50% aneuploid cells in the trophectoderm (TE) – have implantation and birth rates comparable to fully euploid embryos (Capalbo et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published clinical data.

claim: Mouse and human pre-implantation development are highly similar in terms of cleavage divisions, compaction, blastocyst cavity formation, and hatching.
source: Importantly, mouse and human pre-implantation development are highly similar: both undertake cleavage divisions, compaction, blastocyst cavity formation, and hatching, albeit with slightly different timings (Molè et al., 2020; Zhu et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Reversine is a pan-Aurora kinase inhibitor that also antagonizes the A3 adenosine receptor and inhibits mitotic kinase monopolar spindle 1 (MPS1).
source: Reversine is a pan-Aurora kinase inhibitor that also antagonizes the A3 adenosine receptor and inhibits mitotic kinase monopolar spindle 1 (MPS1) (D'Alise et al., 2008; Santaguida et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature on reversine's mechanism of action.

claim: Reversine-treated mosaic embryos exhibit widespread aneuploidy and upregulation of p53.
source: We found that reversine-treated mosaic embryos exhibit widespread aneuploidy and upregulation of p53 (Bolton et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Aneuploid cells in mosaic embryos are progressively eliminated from the EPI, beginning around the time of implantation.
source: Importantly, aneuploid cells in mosaic embryos are progressively eliminated from the EPI, beginning around the time of implantation.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work by the authors.

claim: Murine mosaic embryos containing at least 50% of euploid cells had a similar developmental potential to fully euploid embryos.
source: Consistent with findings in human embryos (Capalbo et al., 2021), murine mosaic embryos containing at least 50% of euploid cells had a similar developmental potential to fully euploid embryos (Bolton et al., 2016; Singla et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work by the authors.

claim: AZ3146 and reversine bind to Mps1 in a different manner.
source: Although both AZ3146 and reversine interfere with the spindle assembly checkpoint, they bind to Mps1 in a different manner (Lan and Cleveland, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: AZ3146 treatment doubled the occurrence of micronuclei in mouse embryos without impairing overall cellular fitness.
source: In mouse embryos, AZ3146 treatment was shown to double the occurrence of micronuclei, indicative of chromosome segregation defects, but without impairing overall cellular fitness (Vázquez-Diez et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The average aneuploidy in DMSO-treated 8-cell embryos was 12.5%, compared to 75% in reversine-treated embryos and 62.5% in AZ3146-treated embryos.
source: After normalization, the average of aneuploidy in DMSO-treated 8-cell embryos was 12.5%, compared to 75% in the reversine-treated embryos and 62.5% in the AZ3146-treated embryos (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by in situ chromosome counting data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: 19% of reversine-treated embryos and 7.9% of AZ3146-treated blastomeres contained nondividing cells, but none were observed in DMSO-treated blastomeres.
source: Specifically, we observed 28 nondividing cells (19%) in reversine-treated embryos and 24 nondividing cells (7.9%) in AZ3146-treated blastomeres, but none in DMSO-treated blastomeres (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: DMSO-treated blastocysts had a median of 93 cells in total, whereas reversine- and AZ3146-treated embryos had a median of only 79 and 82 cells, respectively.
source: We quantified the number of cells in the blastocysts and found that DMSO-treated controls had a median of 93 cells in total, whereas reversine- and AZ3146-treated embryos had a median of only 79 and 82 cells, respectively (n=28 embryos per treatment collected from three independent experiments; Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by cell counting data presented in Figure 1C.

claim: DMSO-treated blastocysts contained a median of 15 EPI, 11 PE, and 67 TE cells.
source: DMSO-treated blastocysts contained a median of 15 EPI, 11 PE, and 67 TE cells, whereas reversine-treated blastocysts contained 12 EPI, 8 PE, and 59 TE cells, and AZ3146-treated blastocysts had 11 EPI, 7 PE, and 64 TE cells (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by lineage-specific cell counting data presented in Figure 1C.

claim: Reversine treatment compromises the development of all three lineages (TE, EPI, and PE).
source: These data suggest that reversine treatment compromises the development of all three lineages, as observed previously (Bolton et al., 2016), whereas AZ3146 mainly compromises ICM (EPI and PE) development (statistical test: Mann–Whitney U-test).
evidence: This is supported by cell counting data and previous publications.

claim: AZ3146 mainly compromises ICM (EPI and PE) development.
source: These data suggest that reversine treatment compromises the development of all three lineages, as observed previously (Bolton et al., 2016), whereas AZ3146 mainly compromises ICM (EPI and PE) development (statistical test: Mann–Whitney U-test).
evidence: This is supported by cell counting data showing reduced EPI and PE cells but not TE cells in AZ3146-treated embryos.

claim: Two (8%) reversine-treated blastocysts developed decidua but none gave rise to viable E9.5 embryos.
source: Although two (8%) reversine-treated blastocysts developed decidua (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C), none gave rise to viable E9.5 embryos.
evidence: This is supported by embryo transfer data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Seven (30%) AZ3146-treated blastocysts developed decidua and five (21%) generated viable E9.5 embryos.
source: In contrast, seven (30%) AZ3146-treated blastocysts developed decidua (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C) and five (21%) generated viable E9.5 embryos (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by embryo transfer data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and 1D.

claim: AZ3146-treated embryos have a higher developmental potential than reversine-treated embryos.
source: Thus, AZ3146-treated embryos appear to have a higher developmental potential than reversine-treated embryos.
evidence: This is inferred from the embryo transfer data showing higher implantation and survival rates for AZ3146-treated embryos.

claim: Elevated γH2A.X levels were observed in reversine- and AZ3146-treated 8-cell embryos compared to controls.
source: We observed elevated γH2A.X levels in reversine- and AZ3146-treated 8-cell embryos compared to controls (Figure 1E) (n=~15 embryos per treatment, ~120 cells. Collection was made during three independent experiments. Statistical test: t-test), which eventually returned to normal in AZ3146-treated blastocysts, but not in reversine-treated blastocysts (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence intensity measurements presented in Figure 1E.

claim: γH2A.X levels returned to normal in AZ3146-treated blastocysts, but not in reversine-treated blastocysts.
source: We observed elevated γH2A.X levels in reversine- and AZ3146-treated 8-cell embryos compared to controls (Figure 1E) (n=~15 embryos per treatment, ~120 cells. Collection was made during three independent experiments. Statistical test: t-test), which eventually returned to normal in AZ3146-treated blastocysts, but not in reversine-treated blastocysts (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data at the blastocyst stage.

claim: PARP1 is specifically enriched in the EPI lineage in normal blastocysts.
source: PARP1 was specifically enriched in the EPI lineage in normal blastocysts, as assessed by IF (n>21 embryos per treatment collected from three independent experiments. Statistical test: Mann–Whitney U-test) and re-analysis of published scRNA-seq data (Deng et al., 2014; GEO accession: GSE45719) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data and scRNA-seq analysis presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: PARP1 levels were reduced at the 8-cell and morula stages in reversine-treated embryos compared to controls and to AZ3146-treated embryos.
source: Intriguingly, PARP1 levels were reduced at the 8-cell and morula stages in reversine-treated embryos compared to controls and to AZ3146-treated embryos (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence intensity measurements presented in Figure 1D and E.

claim: Treatment with olaparib reduced blastocyst cell numbers, particularly in the ICM.
source: Moreover, late morula stage embryos treated with the PARP inhibitor olaparib (10 µM) (Hou et al., 2022; Prasad et al., 2017) developed into smaller blastocysts with only 78 total cells, reflecting a relatively low number of ICM cells, only 8 EPI and 4 PE cells in DMSO-treated embryos (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C–E).
evidence: This is supported by cell counting data from olaparib-treated embryos presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C–E.

claim: Reversine, but not AZ3146, further reduced the number of cells in the EPI lineage of olaparib-treated embryos.
source: Treatment with reversine, but not AZ3146, further reduced the number of cells in the EPI lineage of olaparib-treated embryos (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E) (n=15 embryos per treatment collected from three independent experiments. Statistical test: Mann–Whitney U-test).
evidence: This is supported by lineage analysis data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 2E.

claim: PARP1 is required for proper development of the ICM.
source: Overall, these data suggest that PARP1 is required for proper development of the ICM, and that its reduced levels after reversine treatment may negatively impact development.
evidence: This is inferred from the olaparib treatment experiments showing reduced ICM cell numbers.

claim: Reduced PARP1 levels after reversine treatment may negatively impact development.
source: Overall, these data suggest that PARP1 is required for proper development of the ICM, and that its reduced levels after reversine treatment may negatively impact development.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined observations of reduced PARP1 in reversine-treated embryos and the effects of PARP inhibition.

claim: p53 is frequently activated following DNA damage, which can limit proliferation and trigger apoptosis.
source: For instance, p53 is frequently activated following DNA damage, which can limit proliferation and trigger apoptosis (Abuetabh et al., 2022; Soto et al., 2017; Thompson and Compton, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature on p53 function.

claim: The p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase can be activated following DNA damage.
source: The p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase can also be activated following DNA damage (Thompson and Compton, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: p38 promotes apoptosis by inhibiting the transcription factor Hif-1a in aneuploid cells.
source: In aneuploid cells, p38 promotes apoptosis by inhibiting the transcription factor Hif-1a (Simões-Sousa et al., 2018), which otherwise promotes cell survival, proliferation, and metabolic changes in aneuploid cells and in response to hypoxia in different contexts (Hu et al., 2003; Simões-Sousa et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Hif-1a promotes cell survival, proliferation, and metabolic changes in aneuploid cells and in response to hypoxia.
source: In aneuploid cells, p38 promotes apoptosis by inhibiting the transcription factor Hif-1a (Simões-Sousa et al., 2018), which otherwise promotes cell survival, proliferation, and metabolic changes in aneuploid cells and in response to hypoxia in different contexts (Hu et al., 2003; Simões-Sousa et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Reversine-treated embryos displayed a significant increase in Trp53 transcript levels at the morula (7-fold) and blastocyst (1.3-fold) stages compared with DMSO-treated embryos.
source: Reversine-treated embryos displayed a significant increase in Trp53 transcript levels at the morula (7-fold) and blastocyst (1.3-fold) stages compared with DMSO-treated embryos (sample: three biological replicates and two technical replicates per experiment with each replicate having a minimum of 16 embryos. Statistical test: Welch's t-test) (Figure 2A), as we showed previously (Singla et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data presented in Figure 2A.

claim: Reversine-treated embryos showed reduced expression of Hif1a at the blastocyst stage.
source: In addition, reversine-treated embryos showed reduced expression of Hif1a at the blastocyst stage, which would be consistent with p38 activation.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data presented in Figure 2A.

claim: AZ3146-treated embryos did not show upregulation of Trp53 at either the morula or blastocyst stage.
source: In contrast, AZ3146-treated embryos did not show upregulation of Trp53 at either the morula or blastocyst stage (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data presented in Figure 2A.

claim: AZ3146-treated embryos showed a transient increase in Hif1a mRNA levels (threefold) at the morula stage compared to DMSO- and reversine-treated embryos.
source: Moreover, AZ3146-treated embryos showed a transient increase in Hif1a mRNA levels (threefold) at the morula stage compared to DMSO- and reversine-treated embryos (Figure 2A), which returned to normal levels at the blastocyst stage.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data presented in Figure 2A.

claim: HIF1A protein was elevated at the morula and blastocyst stages in AZ3146-treated embryos.
source: HIF1A protein was present in DMSO- and reversine-treated embryos and elevated at the morula and blastocyst stages in AZ3146-treated embryos (n=~20 embryos per treatment. Statistical test: Mann–Whitney U-test, error bars represent s.e.m.) (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data presented in Figure 2B.

claim: HIF1A appeared to be mostly nuclear in morula, but mostly cytoplasmic in blastocysts, under all three conditions.
source: HIF1A appeared to be mostly nuclear in morula, but mostly cytoplasmic in blastocysts, under all three conditions (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence imaging presented in Figure 2B.

claim: Treatment with reversine, but not AZ3146, induces multiple stress pathways in pre-implantation embryos.
source: Overall, these data suggest that treatment with reversine, but not AZ3146, induces multiple stress pathways in pre-implantation embryos.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential expression of Trp53 and Hif1a in reversine vs. AZ3146-treated embryos.

claim: Differences in stress pathway activation may contribute to the increased developmental potential of embryos treated with AZ3146 versus reversine.
source: These differences may contribute to the increased developmental potential of embryos treated with AZ3146 versus reversine.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the observed differences in stress responses and developmental outcomes.

claim: Hif1a−/− embryos undergo developmental arrest and lethality by E11.
source: It was previously shown that Hif1a−/− embryos undergo developmental arrest and lethality by E11 (Iyer et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: IDF-11774 treatment did not significantly affect the total number of cells in the TE or the whole blastocyst compared to the control.
source: Unlike PX-478, IDF-11774 treatment did not significantly affect the total number of cells in the TE or the whole blastocyst compared to the control (n=~12 embryos per treatment collected from three independent experiments. Statistical test: Mann–Whitney U-test) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by cell counting data presented in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Inhibition of HIF1A dramatically lowered the number of TE and especially PE cells in AZ3146-treated embryos compared to DMSO-treated controls.
source: Inhibition of HIF1A did not abolish cavitation but dramatically lowered the number of TE and especially PE cells in AZ3146-treated embryos compared to DMSO-treated controls (Figure 2D) and compared to AZ3146-treated embryos not exposed to IDF-11884 (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by lineage analysis data presented in Figure 2D.

claim: Inhibition of HIF1A lowered the number of cells in reversine-treated embryos compared to controls, but the effect was smaller than in AZ3146-treated embryos.
source: Inhibition of HIF1A also lowered the number of cells in reversine-treated embryos compared to controls, but the effect was smaller (n=20 embryos per treatment collected from three independent experiments. Statistical test: Mann–Whitney U-test) (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by lineage analysis data presented in Figure 2D.

claim: Elevated HIF1A activity from the 8-cell stage onward is particularly important to promote the survival of aneuploid TE and PE cells after AZ3146 treatment.
source: Overall, our data suggest that elevated HIF1A activity from the 8-cell stage onward is particularly important to promote the survival of aneuploid TE and PE cells after AZ3146 treatment.
evidence: This is inferred from the HIF1A inhibition experiments showing reduced TE and PE cells in AZ3146-treated embryos.

claim: Compared to reversine-treated embryos, AZ3146-treated embryos have increased developmental potential, lack upregulation of Trp53, and show transient upregulation of Hif1a.
source: Taken together, our data suggest that AZ3146 and reversine have distinct effects on the pre-implantation embryo. Compared to reversine-treated embryos, AZ3146-treated embryos appear to have increased developmental potential, lack upregulation of Trp53, and show transient upregulation of Hif1a.
evidence: This is a summary of multiple experimental findings presented in the study.

claim: AZ3146-treated embryos have a greater dependence on HIF1A activity to form the TE and PE.
source: Moreover, AZ3146-treated embryos have a greater dependence on HIF1A activity to form the TE and PE.
evidence: This is inferred from the HIF1A inhibition experiments showing greater effects in AZ3146-treated embryos.

claim: Pre-implantation development occurs in a hypoxic environment.
source: Pre-implantation development occurs in a hypoxic environment, and many clinics culture human embryos under hypoxic conditions (5%) (Houghton, 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature and represents established knowledge.

claim: Physiologic oxygen concentration (~5% oxygen) can improve the yield and quality of mammalian blastocysts.
source: It was reported that physiologic oxygen concentration (~5% oxygen) can improve the yield and quality of mammalian blastocysts (Ciray et al., 2009; Nguyen et al., 2020) and increase the nuclear translocation of HIF1A in mouse blastocysts (Choi et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Physiologic oxygen concentration increases the nuclear translocation of HIF1A in mouse blastocysts.
source: It was reported that physiologic oxygen concentration (~5% oxygen) can improve the yield and quality of mammalian blastocysts (Ciray et al., 2009; Nguyen et al., 2020) and increase the nuclear translocation of HIF1A in mouse blastocysts (Choi et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: DMSO-treated blastocysts cultured under hypoxia had a median of 74 cells, representing 14 EPI cells, 6 PE cells, and 54 TE cells.
source: We found that DMSO-treated blastocysts cultured under hypoxia had a median of 74 cells, representing 14 EPI cells, 6 PE cells, and 54 TE cells (n=18 embryos per treatment collected from three independent experiments. Statistical test: Mann–Whitney U-test) (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: This is supported by cell counting data presented in Figure 3B and C.

claim: The cell number in the pre-implantation mouse blastocyst is reduced when cultured in hypoxia compared to normoxia, particularly in the TE and PE.
source: These data suggest that, under our conditions, the cell number in the pre-implantation mouse blastocyst is reduced when cultured in hypoxia compared to normoxia (Figures 3C and 1C), particularly in the TE and PE.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing cell counts between hypoxia and normoxia conditions.

claim: Reversine and AZ3146 treatment did not further reduce cell numbers for embryos cultured under hypoxia, except for in the PE.
source: Notably, reversine and AZ3146 treatment did not further reduce cell numbers for embryos cultured under hypoxia, except for in the PE (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by lineage analysis data presented in Figure 3C.

claim: Treated embryos with reversine and AZ3146 under hypoxia generated lower levels of γH2A.X compared with the same treatments under normoxia.
source: We found that treated embryos with reversine and AZ3146 under hypoxia generated lower levels of γH2A.X (Figure 3E) compared with the same treatments under normoxia (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by comparing γH2A.X intensity measurements between hypoxia and normoxia conditions.

claim: PARP1 levels at the 8-cell stage are reduced in reversine-treated embryos under hypoxia, similar to normoxic conditions.
source: Whereas PARP1 levels at the 8-cell stage are reduced in reversine-treated embryos (Figure 3E), similar to normoxic conditions (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by PARP1 intensity measurements under hypoxia and normoxia.

claim: At the morula stages, the levels of PARP1 are relatively low compared to morula stage in normoxic conditions.
source: Importantly, at the morula stages, the levels of PARP1 are relatively low compared to morula stage in normoxic conditions (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by comparing PARP1 intensity measurements between hypoxia and normoxia at the morula stage.

claim: Hypoxia exposure lowers the accumulation of DNA damage between the 8-cell to morula stages and results in a reduction of PARP1 at the morula stage.
source: Overall, these data suggest that hypoxia exposure lowers the accumulation of DNA damage between the 8-cell to morula stages and results in a reduction of PARP1 at the morula stage.
evidence: This is inferred from the γH2A.X and PARP1 measurements under hypoxia.

claim: DMSO/AZ3146 and reversine/AZ3146 blastocysts displayed proper lineage allocation, embryo morphology, and cavitation in both normoxia and hypoxia.
source: DMSO/AZ3146 and reversine/AZ3146 blastocysts displayed proper lineage allocation, embryo morphology, and cavitation in both normoxia and hypoxia (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence imaging presented in Figure 4B and C.

claim: DMSO/AZ3146 and reversine/AZ3146 embryos had comparable total cell numbers in their blastocysts.
source: In addition, DMSO/AZ3146 and reversine/AZ3146 embryos had comparable total cell numbers in their blastocysts, and blastocysts grown in hypoxia were again smaller than those grown in normoxia (Figure 4D and E).
evidence: This is supported by cell counting data presented in Figure 4D and E.

claim: Blastocysts grown in hypoxia were smaller than those grown in normoxia.
source: In addition, DMSO/AZ3146 and reversine/AZ3146 embryos had comparable total cell numbers in their blastocysts, and blastocysts grown in hypoxia were again smaller than those grown in normoxia (Figure 4D and E).
evidence: This is supported by cell counting data comparing hypoxia and normoxia conditions.

claim: Despite having fewer total cells, DMSO/AZ3146 blastocysts had more EPI cells when they were cultured in hypoxia compared to normoxia.
source: Intriguingly, despite having fewer total cells, DMSO/AZ3146 blastocysts had more EPI cells when they were cultured in hypoxia compared to normoxia (Figure 4D and E).
evidence: This is supported by lineage-specific cell counting data presented in Figure 4D and E.

claim: In DMSO/AZ3146-treated blastocysts under normoxia, 46.75% of the TE and 42.88% of the EPI originated from AZ3146-treated blastomeres, compared to only 28.57% of the PE.
source: In DMSO/AZ3146-treated blastocysts, we found that 46.75% of the TE and 42.88% of the EPI originated from AZ3146-treated blastomeres, compared to only 28.57% of the PE (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is supported by lineage allocation quantification data presented in Figure 4F.

claim: In reversine/AZ3146 chimeras under normoxia, 63% of the TE and 78.4% of the EPI originated from AZ3146-treated cells, compared to only 40% of the PE.
source: In reversine/AZ3146 chimeras, 63% of the TE and 78.4% of the EPI originated from AZ3146-treated cells, compared to only 40% of the PE (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is supported by lineage allocation quantification data presented in Figure 4F.

claim: Under normoxia, DMSO cells appear to outcompete AZ3146-treated cells, which in turn outcompete reversine-treated cells in the TE and EPI.
source: Thus, under normoxia, DMSO cells appear to outcompete AZ3146-treated cells, which in turn outcompete reversine-treated cells in the TE and EPI.
evidence: This is inferred from the lineage allocation data showing differential contributions of different cell types.

claim: AZ3146-treated cells appeared to be at a competitive disadvantage in the PE in both DMSO/AZ3146 and reversine/AZ3146 contexts under normoxia.
source: AZ3146-treated cells appeared to be at a competitive disadvantage in the PE in both contexts.
evidence: This is inferred from the lower proportion of AZ3146-treated cells in the PE compared to other lineages.

claim: Culturing DMSO/AZ3146 chimeras in hypoxia increased the representation of AZ3146-treated blastomeres in the TE (49.06%) and PE (50%) but reduced their representation in the EPI (33.3%).
source: Culturing DMSO/AZ3146 chimeras in hypoxia increased the representation of AZ3146-treated blastomeres in the TE (49.06%) and PE (50%) but, strikingly, reduced their representation in the EPI (33.3%) (n>7 embryos per treatment collected from three independent experiments. Statistical test: Mann–Whitney U-test) (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is supported by lineage allocation quantification data under hypoxia presented in Figure 4G.

claim: Hypoxia exposure of reversine/AZ3146 embryos lowered the contribution of AZ3146-treated blastomeres to the TE (55.94%) and EPI (50%), but not to the PE (46.43%).
source: Hypoxia exposure of reversine/AZ3146 embryos lowered the contribution of AZ3146-treated blastomeres to the TE (55.94%) and EPI (50%), but not to the PE (46.43%) (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is supported by lineage allocation quantification data under hypoxia presented in Figure 4G.

claim: There was no correlation between the proportion of AZ3146-treated cells in the TE and the EPI in DMSO/AZ3146 and reversine/AZ3146 aggregation chimeras, under hypoxia or normoxia.
source: We found that there was no correlation between the proportion of AZ3146-treated cells in the TE and the EPI in DMSO/AZ3146 and reversine/AZ3146 aggregation chimeras, under hypoxia or normoxia, and that hypoxia seemed to have a greater impact on the proportion of AZ3146 cells in reversine/AZ3146 aggregation chimeras (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis presented in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Hypoxia has lineage-specific effects on competitions between aneuploid and euploid cells and increases the contribution of euploid cells to the EPI.
source: Overall, these data suggest that hypoxia has lineage-specific effects on competitions between aneuploid and euploid cells and increases the contribution of euploid cells to the EPI.
evidence: This is inferred from the lineage allocation data comparing hypoxia and normoxia conditions.

claim: Reversine treatment at the zygote stage strongly affects the morphology of the blastocysts.
source: Importantly, reversine treatment at the zygote stage seems to strongly affect the morphology of the blastocysts (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data presented in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Reversine treatment at the zygote stage reduced the number of cells in all lineages, particularly in the TE and PE.
source: Consistent with this change in morphology, reversine treatment reduced the number of cells in all lineages, particularly in the TE and PE (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by cell counting data presented in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B.

claim: AZ3146 treatment at the zygote stage did not affect morphology or cell number in any of the lineages.
source: In contrast, AZ3146 treatment did not affect morphology or cell number in any of the lineages (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A and B) (n=~27 embryos per treatment collected from three independent experiments. Statistical test: Mann–Whitney U-test).
evidence: This is supported by morphology and cell counting data presented in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: Reversine-treated cells were extruded from the blastocyst in 54% of the reversine/DMSO chimeras and in 33% of the AZ3146/reversine chimeras, whereas no cell extrusion was observed in the DMSO/AZ3146 chimeras.
source: Interestingly, the reversine-treated cells were extruded from the blastocyst in 54% of the reversine/DMSO chimeras and in 33% of the AZ3146/reversine chimeras, whereas no cell extrusion was observed in the DMSO/AZ3146 chimeras.
evidence: This is supported by observations from 2-cell stage aggregation chimeras.

claim: Aneuploidy generated at different stages similarly affects the proportion of aneuploid cells in the blastocysts.
source: Overall, these results suggest that aneuploidy generated at different stages similarly affects the proportion of aneuploid cells in the blastocysts.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing 2-cell and 8-cell stage aggregation chimera results.

claim: Treatment of DMSO/AZ3146 chimeras with IDF11774 does not affect lineage segregation in the blastocyst but reduces the cavity diameter.
source: Treatment of DMSO/AZ3146 chimeras with IDF11774 does not affect lineage segregation in the blastocyst but reduces the cavity diameter (Figure 5B and C).
evidence: This is supported by imaging and cavity diameter measurements presented in Figure 5B and C.

claim: IDF11774 treatment diminishes the contribution of AZ3146-treated cells to the TE, but DMSO-treated cells seem to compensate for this loss in the PE and EPI.
source: Additionally, diminish the contribution of AZ3146-treated cells to the TE, but DMSO-treated cells seem to compensate for this loss in the PE and EPI (Figure 5D, Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by lineage allocation data presented in Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Treating reversine/AZ3146 chimeras with IDF11774 compromised blastocyst morphology and cavitation.
source: Treating reversine/AZ3146 chimeras with IDF11774 compromised blastocyst morphology and cavitation (Figure 5E and F) and considerably increased the number of PE and EPI cells (n>8 embryos per treatment collected from three independent experiments. Statistical test: Mann–Whitney U-test) (Figure 5G), without altering the frequency of AZ3146-treated cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by imaging and cell counting data presented in Figure 5E, F, and G.

claim: HIF1A promotes the survival of AZ3146-treated cells in DMSO/AZ3146 chimeras.
source: Taken together, our data suggest that HIF1A promotes the survival of AZ3146-treated cells in DMSO/AZ3146 chimeras and suggest that inhibiting HIF1A could increase the proportion of karyotypically normal cells in mosaic embryos.
evidence: This is inferred from the IDF11774 treatment experiments showing reduced AZ3146-treated cells.

claim: Inhibiting HIF1A could increase the proportion of karyotypically normal cells in mosaic embryos.
source: Taken together, our data suggest that HIF1A promotes the survival of AZ3146-treated cells in DMSO/AZ3146 chimeras and suggest that inhibiting HIF1A could increase the proportion of karyotypically normal cells in mosaic embryos.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the IDF11774 treatment experiments.

claim: Reversine downregulates PARP1, consistent with previous findings in glioma cells.
source: Our current results further indicate that reversine downregulates PARP1, consistent with previous findings in glioma cells (Hirakata et al., 2021), thereby exacerbating DNA damage and limiting DNA repair capacity.
evidence: This is supported by PARP1 measurements in reversine-treated embryos and a citation to published literature.

claim: Reversine downregulation of PARP1 exacerbates DNA damage and limits DNA repair capacity.
source: Our current results further indicate that reversine downregulates PARP1, consistent with previous findings in glioma cells (Hirakata et al., 2021), thereby exacerbating DNA damage and limiting DNA repair capacity.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined observations of reduced PARP1 and elevated DNA damage in reversine-treated embryos.

claim: Hypoxic culture conditions have been shown to improve the quality of mammalian blastocysts.
source: Indeed, hypoxic culture conditions have been shown to improve the quality of mammalian blastocysts (Ciray et al., 2009; Nguyen et al., 2020), though the underlying mechanisms remain unclear.
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Studies in somatic cells suggest that hypoxia enhances DNA repair pathways.
source: Studies in somatic cells suggest that hypoxia enhances DNA repair pathways (Martí et al., 2021; Nakamura et al., 2022; Pietrzak et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Recent work in cancer cells indicates that hypoxia may promote HIF1A-PARP1 interactions, enhancing DNA repair.
source: Furthermore, recent work in cancer cells indicates that hypoxia may promote HIF1A-PARP1 interactions, enhancing DNA repair (Martí et al., 2021; Nakamura et al., 2022; Pietrzak et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Confined placental mosaicism, in which the placenta is aneuploid while the fetus is euploid, is a common phenomenon in human pregnancies.
source: Confined placental mosaicism, in which the placenta is aneuploid while the fetus is euploid, is a common phenomenon in human pregnancies (McCoy, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Aneuploid TE cells exhibit prolonged cell cycles and signs of senescence in reversine-treated embryos.
source: In previous work, we showed that aneuploid TE cells exhibit prolonged cell cycles and signs of senescence, whereas aneuploid ICM cells have an increased frequency of apoptosis in reversine-treated embryos (Singla et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Aneuploid ICM cells have an increased frequency of apoptosis in reversine-treated embryos.
source: In previous work, we showed that aneuploid TE cells exhibit prolonged cell cycles and signs of senescence, whereas aneuploid ICM cells have an increased frequency of apoptosis in reversine-treated embryos (Singla et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Abnormal, yet viable TE cells may contribute to confined placental mosaicism.
source: These findings suggest that abnormal, yet viable TE cells may contribute to confined placental mosaicism.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the observation of viable aneuploid TE cells.

claim: In AZ3146-treated embryos cultured under normoxic conditions, aneuploid cells contributed predominantly to the TE, followed by the EPI, and were especially depleted from the PE.
source: In the present study, we found that in AZ3146-treated embryos cultured under normoxic conditions, aneuploid cells contributed predominantly to the TE, followed by the EPI, and were especially depleted from the PE.
evidence: This is supported by lineage allocation data from chimeric embryos.

claim: Under hypoxic conditions, aneuploid cells were more frequently eliminated from the EPI and enriched in the PE.
source: Under hypoxic conditions, however, we observed a shift: aneuploid cells were more frequently eliminated from the EPI and enriched in the PE.
evidence: This is supported by lineage allocation data from chimeric embryos cultured in hypoxia.

claim: The proportions of aneuploid cells in the TE and EPI do not correlate.
source: Moreover, we confirmed that the proportions of aneuploid cells in the TE and EPI do not correlate, consistent with the preferential survival of aneuploid cells in the TE and their selective elimination from the ICM.
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis presented in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: There is low concordance of aneuploidy between TE and ICM in human mosaic embryos (30–40%).
source: This is in line with clinical data showing low concordance of aneuploidy between TE and ICM in human mosaic embryos (30–40%) (Dahdouh and Garcia-Velasco, 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published clinical data.

claim: Lineage-specific elimination of aneuploid cells by apoptosis has been described in an in vitro model of human post-implantation development using reversine.
source: Lineage-specific elimination of aneuploid cells by apoptosis has been described in an in vitro model of human post-implantation development using reversine (Yang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Mechanisms of DNA repair involving PARP1 and HIF1A may underlie the differential survival of aneuploid cells across lineages.
source: Our findings mirror this distinction and further suggest that mechanisms of DNA repair – possibly involving PARP1 and HIF1A – may underlie the differential survival of aneuploid cells across lineages.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the observed roles of PARP1 and HIF1A in the study.

claim: Treatment with the HIF1A inhibitor IDF-11774 increased the proportion of euploid cells in mosaic embryos.
source: In this study, we targeted HIF1A as a potential regulator of aneuploid cell persistence and found that treatment with the HIF1A inhibitor IDF-11774 increased the proportion of euploid cells in mosaic embryos.
evidence: This is supported by lineage allocation data from IDF-11774-treated chimeric embryos.

claim: Specific environmental and molecular factors can modulate the composition of mosaic embryos.
source: Taken together, our findings reveal that specific environmental and molecular factors can modulate the composition of mosaic embryos, with potential implications for improving embryo quality and reproductive outcomes.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the findings regarding hypoxia and HIF1A inhibition.
